elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 still binds Ono: "neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory" any Competing Product, and the redline narrows rather than deletes that covenant (new sentence caps it at twelve months instead of removing it). The preferred position is therefore expressly not taken.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Pre-existing definition confines the covenant to a product class: "(i) a product that includes, as an active pharmaceutical ingredient, an agent that is a [ * ] (other than Binimetinib), or (ii) ... (other than Encorafenib) ... (each a \"Competing Product\")". No edit was needed and none was made to this element.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The obligations of Ono and its Affiliates under this Section 8.2 shall in no event continue beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date". The cap is drafted against all Ono obligations "under this Section 8.2", so it also caps the redacted post-termination tail ("prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect"), and the "in no event" override resolves the conflict with that retained sentence.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "shall terminate automatically if Array fails to meet its supply obligations under Article 9 of this Agreement, including any service levels ... agreed by the Parties or set forth in any supply agreement entered into pursuant to Article 9." The trigger is self-executing ("terminate automatically") and anchored to Array's existing Article 9 supply obligations, so it is operable even if no separate supply agreement or service-level schedule is executed.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence expressly names "delivery dates agreed by the Parties or set forth in any supply agreement entered into pursuant to Article 9" as an included Article 9 supply obligation whose breach automatically terminates Ono's covenant.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the covenant is already category-limited to "Competing Product", and the inserted sentence supplies all three missing elements (a hard twelve-month outer limit and automatic termination on Array's supply/service-level/delivery-date failure) in operative language rather than in the comment.

Preferred level is not met and is not claimed: the exclusivity obligation on Ono survives in narrowed form, which is the correct redline-to-fallback outcome for what was otherwise walk-away territory (full-term exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit).

Minimality holds. The insertion is a single conforming sentence addressed only to the three unmet elements; the category limb, Array's reciprocal covenant (which benefits Ono and must be kept), the royalty-termination mechanic on Array's competition, and the Section 13.2/13.3 references are all left intact. Anchoring the exit to "supply obligations under Article 9" is necessary rather than decorative, because this pharma licence contains no standalone "service levels" construct and an unanchored trigger would be undefined.

The second operation ("in breach of this Section 8.2" replacing "during [ * ]" in Array's immediate-termination right) is a permissible conforming edit, not an extra: without it the Agreement would retain a sentence letting Array terminate for Ono's competition after the capped covenant has expired, which would contradict the new cap and de facto extend the exclusivity.

Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created, the redacted tail is subordinated by an express "in no event" override rather than deleted, and Array's obligations, remedies and the parties' commercial allocation are otherwise untouched.

Residual point for the drafter (not a failure): the service-level/delivery-date limb is phrased conditionally ("agreed by the Parties or set forth in any supply agreement"). If Array pushes back, consider tightening to "any failure by Array to supply conforming Product in the quantities and by the dates required under Article 9" so the exit cannot be argued to depend on a schedule that was never agreed.
